ABOUT MERCOR



Mercor’s mission is to organize human intelligence for the AI economy. We build the infrastructure that enables frontier AI labs and enterprises to train, evaluate, and improve AI on real-world professional work. More than five million experts have joined our network, and we pay out over $5 million daily for their knowledge and expertise.

We built our training and evaluation infrastructure alongside the world’s leading AI labs. Now, we’re bringing those capabilities to enterprises across industries, enabling them to train, evaluate, and improve AI using their own expertise and standards. Our APEX benchmarks measure how AI performs on economically valuable work, while our enterprise evaluations and post-training capabilities turn those insights into measurable improvements across real-world workflows.

Our work sits at the intersection of frontier AI, human expertise, and real-world application. We’re solving problems few companies have encountered, with the opportunity to influence what the world’s most advanced AI systems become capable of doing. We’re looking for people who bring different perspectives, take ownership, exercise sound judgment, and hold themselves to an exceptionally high standard. You’ll have the opportunity to do consequential work alongside talented colleagues who challenge one another, collaborate openly, and share a commitment to excellence.

Mercor is profitable and recently raised a $750 million Series D at a $20 billion valuation. We work in person five days a week in San Francisco, New York, and London.







ABOUT THE ROLE

As a Backend Software Engineer, Infrastructure at Mercor, you'll design and build the core services and platforms that the rest of engineering builds on. You'll work closely with engineers across product, research, and operations to turn hard scaling problems into well-designed, well-tested software.



This is a software engineering role first. You'll spend most of your time designing systems, writing and reviewing code for services, platforms, and tooling that the rest of engineering builds on, ensuring they hold up in production at scale.

We're hiring across Infrastructure: Platform, Developer Platform, Storage and Databases. We team-match after the first screen, so apply even if your background leans toward one area.


WHAT YOU'LL WORK ON

 - Design and build multi-tenant platform services that give dozens of teams isolated capacity, routing, quotas, and observability on demand, owned from architecture review through production.

 - Scale the gateway that fronts every model provider we use, so internal teams and products get reliable, fair, cost-aware access to inference without filing a ticket.

 - Build the internal platforms and APIs that product and research engineers rely on every day, and treat them with the same design and testing rigor as customer-facing code.

 - Design data models, storage layers, and workflows on Postgres, MongoDB, and Temporal that hold up at the next 10x, including schema evolution, sharding and partitioning strategies, and migrations.

 - Build developer-facing platform components (sandboxes, job execution, service frameworks) where coding agents are first-class users alongside humans.

 - Write design docs, lead architecture reviews, and set the patterns for how services at Mercor handle concurrency, retries, idempotency, and backpressure.

 - Improve the performance and efficiency of hot paths, and make architectural changes that bend the cost curve.


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

We care far more about how you reason about systems than which tools you've used. Strong candidates typically have:

 - Strong software engineering fundamentals: you design systems before you build them, write code you're proud of in Python or Go, test it, and review others' code with care.

 - A deep grasp of distributed systems fundamentals: consistency, concurrency, failure modes, backpressure, idempotency, and capacity planning.

 - Experience designing APIs and services used by other engineers, and evolving them without breaking their consumers.

 - Solid experience with relational and/or document databases: data modeling, query performance, and safe migrations.

 - Working familiarity with cloud infrastructure (we're on AWS) and containers. Deep Terraform or Kubernetes expertise is not required; you need to be curious and fast to pick it up.

 - High ownership: you see a gap, write the proposal, ship it, and stand behind it in production.


YOU MIGHT BE A GREAT FIT IF

 - You're a backend engineer who keeps getting pulled toward the platform layer because that's where the hardest problems are.

 - You've built internal platforms, SDKs, or shared services that other engineers loved using.

 - You've worked on multi-tenant systems, rate limiting and quota systems, API gateways, or LLM/inference serving.

 - You've used databases, message queues, or workflow engines at meaningful scale and understand their tradeoffs from the inside.


NICE TO HAVE

 - Experience building developer experience tooling, such as CI pipelines, build systems, local development environments, or internal CLIs that make engineers faster.

 - Interest in contributing to developer productivity work alongside your core focus: cutting CI time, improving test reliability, or building sandboxes and guardrails for coding agents.


HOW WE WORK

 - Small, senior team with direct access to the Head of Infrastructure and to engineering leadership.

 - In-person five days a week in SF. Infra is a team sport for us.

 - We use AI coding agents heavily and expect you to as well; the interesting work is deciding what they should do, not typing.

 - Weekly on-call rotation with structured handoffs; on-call load is a metric we actively drive down.
